close_reason: Premise corrected. The def-head 'macro bounce' is NOT a no-op identity round-trip: the runtime macros (src/modules/runtime_library/runtime.fz:40-58) wrap each def-head in Fz.Compiler.define(source, __CALLER__), capturing the lexical environment. This is Elixir-aligned — defmodule/def/defprotocol/defimpl are Kernel macros that capture __CALLER__/__ENV__ and emit a compiler-internal call (elixir/lib/elixir/lib/kernel.ex:5163/5382/5732/5743 -> :elixir_module.compile(..., __ENV__)). The ScopeSurfaceMode flag is therefore a SYMPTOM of a deeper alignment gap, not a removable local smell: fz structurally pre-parses def-heads into typed ScopeForms at read time (a step Elixir does not have), and the mode toggles whether a def-head reads as a MacroCall (user source) or a typed definition (post-expansion/reserved fragment). Reframed and superseded by the new top-level alignment-gap ticket.
description: build_form switches on ScopeSurfaceMode: in Source mode a def-head (defmodule/defprotocol/defimpl/fn) becomes a MacroCall that expands via a runtime macro re-emitting the same quoted node, which is then read in CompilerFragment mode to parse directly. The mode flag exists only to stop that round-trip from recursing. The macro expansion of a def-head is a no-op identity round-trip. Investigate collapsing the two modes — source should be source; a def-head should parse once without a mode-gated macro bounce. Flagged during fz-hwn.19.2.4.16 (Elixir-aligned protocol dispatch).
title: Source-form 'modes' (ScopeSurfaceMode::Source vs CompilerFragment) are a smell
